title: Letter No. 937 — response to two letters and two panim; positive thought and speech regarding illness
response_propositions: The response promises to read petitions for the recipient's wife and grandson at the Previous Rebbe's gravesite and expresses hope for their recovery.
It criticizes severe or exaggerated speech and writing about illness, extending the maxim of positive thought to spoken and written expression.
The closing interpretation frames faith as capable of gaining mastery over bodily and worldly obstacles and transforming opposition toward good.
proposition_source_locator: publisher translation, lines 279-287: petitions, illness language, positive thought and closing Purim interpretation
verification_scope: The authorized publisher's English translation was inspected. Propositions are bounded paraphrases; the enclosed petitions, diagnoses, incoming letters, physical original and original-language witness were not inspected. This is historical-source description, not medical advice.
documented_circumstances: Letter No. 937 to R. Yisrael Noach Bilenitzky, dated first day of Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5711, responding to two undated letters and two enclosed petitions.
primary_secondary_status: authorized publisher English translation by Eli Touger; derived, non-independent witness
rights_status: copyrighted-source; bounded research paraphrases and link only; no protected full text copied
summary_researcher: Published correspondence page identifies the recipient as R. Yisrael Noach Bilenitzky and states that the letter responds to two undated letters and two enclosed panim. The response includes assurance that the panim will be read at the Rebbe Rayatz's gravesite and guidance against severe/exaggerated speech about illness, explicitly invoking 'Tracht gut, vet zain gut'. The incoming letters and panim are not present on the public page, so the initiating situation remains only partially recoverable.
